answer: One concrete defense is a slow, locked stake per identity: like a glacier, the deposit moves only after a long delay, so creating thousands of fake accounts ties up capital and time no attacker wants to spend. The stake is bound to a single hardware-backed credential, a hard shell like a walnut, cheap to verify but costly to forge in bulk. And a public ledger works like a crystal: every stake and its history are visible, so duplicate identities and coordinated bursts stand out at once and peers can slash or ignore them.
